text: Assessment and post-certification tightened to ensure quality of five-star OCOP products

HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam is tightening assessment and post-certification inspections of its five-star One Commune One Product (OCOP) programme to improve product quality, ensure compliance with standards and strengthen the competitiveness of locally made goods in domestic and international markets.

At a review session on November 18 in Hà Nội, the Central OCOP Evaluation Council approved 12 of 16 products submitted for a new national five-star rating, while the remaining four must provide further explanations and supporting documents.
All 20 products submitted for re-evaluation also passed, reflecting increasingly stringent requirements for maintaining the quality and value of nationally certified OCOP products.

Among the newly approved products, four come from the Suối Giàng Tourism Ecosystem Cooperative in Văn Chấn Commune, Lào Cai Province, namely Vietnam Teashop Suối Giàng White Tea, Yellow Tea, Red Tea and Diệp Tea.

Following the latest assessment, dossiers for all 32 products will be finalised by the central coordinating office of the National Target Programmes and submitted to the Minister of Agriculture and Environment for consideration and official recognition.

Nguyễn Xuân Đại, the council's deputy chairman, said that after eight years of implementation, Việt Nam had developed more than 21,000 OCOP products rated three stars or higher by November 2026, involving 10,657 participating entities.
However, only 166 products had achieved the national five-star rating, indicating substantial room to improve quality and increase the value of Vietnamese OCOP products.
OCOP products are expected not only to serve domestic consumers but also to meet export standards, helping enhance brand credibility and the reputation of Vietnamese goods in international markets.
Under new regulations, the five-star certification process places greater emphasis not only on initial assessment but also on post-certification inspections.

Producers must commit to maintaining consistent quality, ensuring food safety and complying with technical standards throughout production and business operations, rather than focusing solely on completing documentation at the time of application.
The approach is intended to make the five-star OCOP designation a measure of competitiveness and sustainable commercial value in the marketplace.
The list of products awarded national five-star OCOP status is expected to be officially announced at the Việt Nam OCOP Festival 2026, scheduled for December 3 in HCM City. - VNS
